c.tagline: Thuringia's medieval capital, where an inhabited bridge crosses the Gera and Luther studied.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; you can hail on the street, wait at a rank, or book by phone or app. Ride-hailing apps FreeNow, Uber and Bolt also operate.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number for ambulance and fire; 110 reaches the police. Both are free and staffed by English-speaking operators.

hood_desc: One of Germany's largest and best-preserved medieval old towns, threaded by the Gera river and centred on the Fischmarkt; home to the Kraemerbruecke — Europe's longest inhabited bridge, still lined with shops and houses — plus the Mariendom and St. Severi churches on their hill; best for first-timers who want the historic core on foot.

The old craftsmen's quarter northwest of the centre, a warren of narrow lanes and half-timbered houses that survived the war, now dotted with small hotels, wine bars and workshops; atmospheric, quiet and central, popular with those wanting old-Erfurt charm.

A leafy 19th-century district south of the old town toward the Steigerwald forest, with villas, the Egapark gardens nearby and easy tram links; a calm, green residential base within reach of the sights.

A quiet residential quarter southwest of the centre near the Theater Erfurt, the Bruehler Garten and the Augustinian riverside, with parks and local eateries; suits travellers wanting a relaxed, less touristy stay close to the old town.

Erfurt's grand central boulevard and main shopping and transport hub, lined with Wilhelmine department stores, the Angermuseum and cafes, and the meeting point of most tram lines; a convenient, lively base right at the city's crossroads.

water.note: Tap water is high quality and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 4:30am to around 11:30pm, with a Nightliner network on Friday and Saturday nights.
transit.pay: No tap-in gates: buy tickets in the EVAG app, at machines, or from the driver, and validate before boarding; one ticket covers EVAG trams and buses across the VMT network. A single ride is about €2.30 (~$2.50) and a day ticket about €5.90. Staying weeks? The €58/month Deutschland-Ticket covers local transit nationwide.

bus: Erfurt ZOB (Central Bus Station, at the Hauptbahnhof)

transit.m: Tram line 4 to city centre / Anger (~15 min, every 10-15 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law; locals round the bill up to the next euro or add about 5-10% for good service, handed to the server rather than left on the table.
